title: Litmus Oracle: Canary + Automated Rollback Harness for Cost-Driven Batch/Cache Changes
creator: Aisha Reddy
description: Build an automated canary and rollback harness ("Litmus Oracle") that validates batching and KV-cache configuration changes against an acceptance suite of golden prompts and task-specific metrics before applying cost-saving optimizations broadly.
background: We frequently propose batch/cache config changes that reduce per-token cost but sometimes cause subtle quality regressions (hallucination, truncation, context-loss) for certain prompt archetypes. Current manual canary runs are time-consuming and inconsistent. Past incidents indicate regressions are frequently only visible on small golden prompt sets or via task-specific metrics rather than token-level heuristics.
goals: 1) Create a reproducible canary flow that runs candidate config changes against a curated eval harness of golden prompts and synthetic probes. 2) Automate statistical checks and deterministic rollback triggers. 3) Integrate the harness into the config apply pipeline so production changes require a green Litmus Oracle before >10% rollout.
non_goals: 1) Replacing human review for complex semantic regressions. 2) Building new model-level evals for every customer feature.
proposed_solution:
- Author a standardized golden prompt corpus (100-300 prompts) covering: conversational stateful prompts, long-context summarization, instruction-following edge cases, few-shot examples, and embedding stability probes.
- Implement a canary runner that can run candidate configs in three modes: shadow (no traffic), dry-canary (synthetic traffic), and live-canary (weighted production traffic up to 10%).
- Compute a set of quantitative metrics per prompt: embedding cosine drift, semantic similarity (BERT/SimCSE), exact-match for structured output, hallucination flag rate, length distribution shift, latency (p50/p95/p99), and cost delta.
- Apply statistical tests per metric: paired bootstrap for similarity, McNemar for categorical pass/fail checks, and concomitant p-value thresholds (default alpha=0.05) plus minimum absolute delta guardrails.
- Define a roll/rollback automaton: if any high-priority metric breaches absolute threshold or statistical significance with effect size >X, trigger automatic rollback and notify owners.
- Integrate results into the Console: per-candidate detailed report, diff visualization, and one-click rollback link.
acceptance_criteria: Litmus Oracle can run a full golden prompt suite in shadow mode against a candidate batching/cache config within 45 minutes for a 100-prompt corpus.
Automated checks flag regressions based on combined criteria: (p < 0.05 AND abs(delta) > 3 percentage points) for binary metrics or (p < 0.05 AND Cohen's d > 0.2) for continuous metrics.
Live-canary rollout is gated: candidate config must pass shadow and dry-canary gates before any production traffic is routed.
Automated rollback will revert the config within 5 minutes of a triggered guardrail and post a reproducible failure report to the change ticket and Slack channel.
Console shows per-prompt diffs for top-10 regressions and a single aggregate pass/fail verdict exported to PRs and deployment logs.
test_plan: Implement unit tests for metric computation (embedding drift, similarity).
Create synthetic failure modes (truncate context, inject hallucination patterns) and verify Litmus Oracle catches them via the harness.
Run end-to-end pipeline on a canary cluster with two recent candidate configs: one safe, one intentionally regressive. Verify rollbacks fire only for the regressive case.
Perform A/B statistical validation on historical rollouts (replay) to estimate false positive/negative rates and calibrate thresholds.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal shadow runs only with engineering traffic (Week 0-2). Phase 2: dry-canary with synthetic traffic from canary harness and nightly batch runs (Week 2-4). Phase 3: live-canary at 1%->5%->10% traffic escalation with automated hold/rollback gates (Week 4-6). Post-mortem and threshold tuning after initial live canaries.
revert_playbook: 1) Automated rollback triggers revert operation and annotate deployment. 2) Pager to on-call and assignee. 3) Run targeted replay on failing prompts and attach trace IDs. 4) Open an investigation ticket with top-10 regressed prompts and metric deltas. 5) If recurring, pin config and schedule a joint triage with Model Ops and Research.
risk_analysis:
- False negatives: low chance for semantic regressions not covered by golden corpus. Mitigation: expand golden set and periodic sampling.
- False positives: overly sensitive thresholds could block safe optimizations. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and staged escalation.
- Cost: additional compute for shadow/dry runs; cap frequency and reuse cached KV where possible.
notes: This harness should be compatible with both hosted and dedicated clusters; private deployments may opt out of telemetry exports but can still run the harness locally.
Coordination required with Infra to reserve canary GPU pools and with Observability to add new dashboards.
